candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies; safely administer parenteral medications, evaluate response, and educate clients about injection technique
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — insulin injection-site rotation and lipodystrophy
candidate.educational_objective: Teach insulin users to avoid lipodystrophic or lumpy injection areas, rotate injection sites appropriately, and monitor glucose closely when moving injections from affected to unaffected tissue because insulin absorption may change.

options.A: Stop injecting into the abnormal area, rotate sites within an appropriate region, and monitor glucose more closely when changing to unaffected tissue.
options.B: Continue using the lumpy area because lipodystrophy improves insulin absorption and reduces glucose variability.
options.C: Massage the thickened area immediately after each injection so insulin enters the bloodstream more rapidly.
options.D: Use only the same exact skin spot for each dose because changing sites is the main cause of lipodystrophy.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current insulin labeling instructs clients to rotate injection sites to reduce lipodystrophy and localized cutaneous amyloidosis and to avoid injecting into areas that are thickened, pitted, or lumpy. Repeated injections into affected tissue have been associated with hyperglycemia, while a sudden change from affected to unaffected tissue can increase the risk of hypoglycemia; closer glucose monitoring is therefore appropriate during the change. B and D reverse the purpose of site rotation. C is not a recommended strategy for correcting abnormal injection-site tissue and introduces unpredictable absorption rather than addressing the cause.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Insulin injection sites should be rotated and abnormal lipodystrophic/amyloid areas avoided; moving from chronically affected tissue to unaffected tissue can alter insulin effect and requires closer glucose monitoring.
candidate.source_locator: Dosage and Administration, Section 2.1 — rotate sites within the same region to reduce lipodystrophy/localized cutaneous amyloidosis and avoid affected skin; Warnings and Precautions — repeated injections into affected areas reported with hyperglycemia and sudden change to unaffected areas reported with hypoglycemia
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration
candidate.stem: A client who uses subcutaneous insulin reports repeatedly injecting into the same thickened, lumpy area because the injections feel less painful there. Which teaching is most appropriate?
